Francis Lawrence, director of Netflix’s BioShock movie, opened up to IGN about his favorite video games of all time, and we have to admit that he knows ball.

You might know Lawrence from his work on the Hunger Games films. He's directed almost every single one of them, after all, most recently lending his talents to the upcoming prequel film Sunrise on the Reaping , which hits theaters this November.

With a slew of blockbuster adaptations under his belt, Lawrence is now helming the live-action BioShock movie at Netflix — a project that's nearly 20 years in the making. Given he’s a self-professed fan of the series, we had to ask about his favorite games of all time.

"Well, the big ones for me were Metal Gear Solid , BioShock, and Call of Duty, " he answered. "I'd say the original GTA . I don't think I played beyond the original GTA, but the original one was pretty wild when that came out, the sort of technology of it. But I think those were all kind of my favorites."

When we brought up the imminent release of GTA 6 — arguably the most technologically advanced game in the franchise and one of the most highly anticipated pop culture launches of all time — Lawrence bemoaned how close the game's release is to Sunrise on the Reaping.
"Unfortunately, I think it comes out right around the same time our movie does. Hopefully, people find time for both. Play GTA, go see our movie, play more GTA," he joked.

We got the chance to chat with Lawrence about his BioShock movie , which he said was initially brought to him by Gore Verbinski back in 2009. However, due to scheduling conflicts, he wasn’t able to take the project. Guillermo del Toro was later in talks to direct the film, but "didn’t see eye-to-eye" with the game’s creator, as Lawrence put it.

The version of events that Guillermo del Toro gave to us, however, was far less mild. "We had a very contentious call about a couple of games," he told us as part of our IGN30 Icons interview series. "...So adapting it, BioShock, we had a couple of calls. They are probably one of the most disastrous calls I've ever had. So no, f**k no."

Lawrence is also gearing up to direct a film adaptation of Red Rising , a young adult book series written by author Peirce Brown. That project, too, has been in development hell, but finally found a home at Paramount and a writer to pen the script.

《Ghost of Yotei Dev Sucker Punch》遭遇裁员，领导层着眼于下一个 PlayStation 项目

content.v: https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2025/09/25/scwk6j-1758769803399.jpg
Ghost of Yotei developer Sucker Punch has laid off some staff, just a little over a year after the release of its last game.

Aftermath reported that the studio let 26 employees go, just weeks after Ghost of Yotei's DLC and Complete Edition were released on PS5. The studio has roughly 200 employees as it stands. Aftermath shared an email that was sent out to the team from studio leadership, which reveals that "challenges in the market" and changes in the scope of the team for its next project were the deciding factors in the layoffs.

“After carefully observing the challenges in the market and reviewing the team needs for our next project, we've decided to make some staffing reductions. Several positions across Sucker Punch will be eliminated as a result," the email reads.
The note also stated that they will discuss the plans for the studio's future next week.

”We know this is a lot to take in, and we want to assure you that we did not make this decision lightly. We have given this a lot of attention and worked to support our affected colleagues during this transition as well as we can. … There's no getting around that this is a hard day. Next week we will go into more details about the future.”

As of right now, it's unclear what Sucker Punch's next game will be; it does sound like there is another project in the cards based on the studio's statement. Some want a return to Infamous, whether through a collection of remasters/remakes or a brand-new entry. Others want a new Sly Cooper. And of course, there's appetite for more games in the studio's Ghost series. It wouldn't be surprising if at least one of these happens, as new IP with a big AAA budget is becoming harder and harder to justify.

Ghost of Yotei was one of the biggest games of fall 2025, selling 3.3 million copies in its first month . It's also one of the best-reviewed PS5 exclusives to date. It was also expected to come to PC at some point, but unfortunately, that plan was scrapped when Sony opted to move away from PC . The game recently got a Complete Edition , which added a brand-new story DLC and other additional content. It's unclear if this moved any significant copies or if the audience for the game already capped out with its initial release.

The layoffs also come during a tumultuous time for PlayStation, which has been upsetting fans over its controversial shift to an all-digital future starting in 2028 . The company will phase out physical copies of games in favor of digital releases, likely beginning with PS6. PlayStation also shuttered Bluepoint , a beloved studio that was best known for high-quality remasters, ports, and remakes such as Demon's Souls for PS5. Additionally, PlayStation attempted to scrap development on Hideo Kojima's next gen game, Physint, until Microsoft swooped in to save it .

content.v: https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2026/10/26/save-mass-effect-billboard-times-square-2-1793032285351.png
Mass Effect fans have bought a #SaveMassEffect billboard in Times Square after EA shut down BioWare last week, but the fight to save the sci-fi RPG franchise isn't stopping there.

Whether New York City residents are familiar with Commander Shepard's fight against the Reapers or not, everyone in Times Square was alerted to #SaveMassEffect when its billboard went up today. It's the latest in a string of moves from the community backing the sci-fi RPG franchise and its developers as they work to give them a second wind.

"Keelah si'yah," text on the billboard said. It's a reference to the in-universe language of Khelish, which is spoken by the Quarian species. According to the Mass Effect Wiki , the line specifically translates to "by the homeworld I hope to find one day."

🚨 WE'RE IN TIMES SQUARE! Together with @kalaelizabeth, we've managed to get a #SaveMassEffect billboard up in Times Square, NYC, all day today! 📍 1560 Broadway, above the Pelé store (Duffy Square) ⏰ 15 seconds every hour at :35 HOLD THE LINE! ❤️ https://t.co/wNP9Ak9Vh8

Those supporting #SaveMassEffect come from all over, but the billboard featured in Times Square on this late-October day came from a smaller group known as We Are Mass Effect, a community dedicated to paying tribute to the franchise started in summer 2025 by a 27-year-old in Spain named Ariel Peña Aguilar . He, along with his second-in-command, Mer , as well as X/Twitter user Kala Elizabeth , sought to publish the billboard in hopes of drawing attention to their cause.

The idea originally came from Aguilar and Mer before Elizabeth was brought in for assistance and is part of their goal to keep Mass Effect alive. So far, their efforts include emailing EA directly, contacting Canadian politicians , and doing everything they can to draw more attention to their cause. The best part? Their Times Square billboard is just the beginning.

Aguilar told IGN that community organization around canceled Star Wars project The Hunt for Ben Solo is partly what inspired his push to save Mass Effect. He added, "I thought something like that could work really well for our situation, too."

Our beloved @drowwpoison, co-ceo of We Are Mass Effect, who's been working incredibly hard to give the #SaveMassEffect movement even more power, went to see our billboard in Times Square, New York City! ❤️ ✍️ Sign the petition: https://t.co/AhcEFDBbd0 https://t.co/69jfSoxyci

"At first, I thought it might be a bit of a crazy idea," Aguilar said of the billboard, "but then I brought it up with my project partner, Mer, and the incredible content creator Kala Elizabeth, without whom none of this would have been possible. We all agreed it was worth doing, and we started organizing everything. And we have more plans! The billboard is just the first step."

There's a natural question that comes up whenever there's a grassroots push like this: How much does it cost to put up a billboard in Times Square? Well, at least on a Monday in October, it's only about $250. Both Aguilar and Elizabeth confirmed the financial cost of boosting #SaveMassEffect wasn't the issue. Instead, it was copyright hangups that gave them more trouble than anything, even if it's now a "fun anecdote," according to Aguilar.

"We initially had someone else make a different graphic, but it said 'BioWare' in it, so we had to change it last minute because of copyright," Elizabeth told us. "There was a lot of back-and-forth in a rush to fix it, and I had to remake it myself. I did end up using the wrong Mass Effect saying because I've been thinking about the author Catherynne Valente, who announced she had been working on Mass Effect 5 , and she had written a previous novel about the Quarian ark for Andromeda. Keelah si'yah is that ark. It's still somewhat fitting of the intent, but we mean keelah se'lai. Oops."
Lots of great feedback in the comments. Our next billboard will be simpler and include a QR code to the petition!

As if there was ever any doubt, there are millions of people who still care about Mass Effect. Aguilar clarified that We Are Mass Effect isn't directly affiliated with the major petition going around, even if they do "fully support the petition and the effort behind it." For him, they are "simply fans trying to use every tool and resource at our disposal to support the cause and make sure this movement continues for as long as possible."
Aguilar sees the joint effort as "a message of unity" in the aftermath of decisions made by EA "that goes far beyond our concern for Mass Effect or Dragon Age." This is about more than video games.

"At the end of the day," Aguilar added, "these franchises are works of art, and while they mean an enormous amount to us, we're also deeply concerned about all the developers who have lost their jobs, as well as those who may still face layoffs in the future, especially during such a difficult period for the video game industry."

He continued: "They're the ones who deserve our support the most. We're going to hold the line." It should be said, though, that no one here is under the illusion that EA has any intention of changing course – or even listening.

As Mass Effect fans work together for another trip among the stars, dissenting opinions have seen naysayers push back against any hope at a revival. Aguilar mentioned the billboard team is "familiar with EA's track record when it comes to how they treat their IPs and developers," adding, "it's easy to understand why fans would feel defeated from the outset." Even if expecting change from EA is a "naïve and unrealistic expectation," they'll continue to push forward anyway.

"Unfortunately, I think we all know that EA probably does not care," Elizabeth added, "but amidst all the horrible press right now around EA's new owners, Jared Kushner and the Saudi government , I hope their track record of killing games becomes another topic of the conversation. This is, albeit, just a small part of the corrupt government and sports washing conversation around EA's new owners, but is absolutely part of it.
The #SaveMassEffect petition just hit 200,000! Absolutely insane work by everyone, keep it up! ♥️ https://t.co/tHiNeNhmCt

"SaveMassEffect is also about trying to save media. History. BioWare was a pillar of Edmonton for 30 years, and EA bought them out and shut them down like they have done for now 20 studios. I don't want them to sit on IPs and let them die. Mass Effect, Dragon Age, and Dead Space are just a few, and they all deserve better. What happens when this massive debt they've accrued closes EA, too? Then what?

"This is about the preservation of media and preserving the work of the studios that EA keeps killing. We don't even know if EA let BioWare try to buy themselves out or let someone else buy them before they closed the studio, canceled the game, and fired the 50 employees keeping BioWare together. What they're doing is wrong. BioWare deserved better. The employees deserved better, and the fans deserve better, too.

"We are probably looking at a future where EA is going to sit on these IPs while they let them die but still make merchandise of Commander Shepard. All while Andrew Wilson collects his massive yearly bonuses and lets EA turn into an esports-only company controlled by the Saudi government."

https://img.3dmgame.com/uploads/images/news/20261027/1793064642_649956_jpg_r.jpg
消息称，此次发行可能筹集至少1000亿美元，公司估值或达到1.5万亿至2万亿美元，并可能超过SpaceX在6月上市时创下的纪录。高盛和摩根士丹利被列为主要承销商，交易时间据称瞄准11月16日当周。不过，募资规模、估值及时间均未成为最终条款。
申报材料首次披露部分财务数据。Anthropic在2026年上半年实现营收163亿美元，高于上年同期的11.6亿美元；同期净亏损807亿美元，其中约724亿美元来自可转换票据及类似工具价值变化产生的非现金费用，经营亏损为6.93亿美元。
Anthropic表示，年度消费至少10万美元的客户已超过11900家，公司持有约1317亿美元现金及短期投资。其算力承诺包括与Google最高1145亿美元、与Amazon至少1100亿美元的安排，以及AMD Instinct MI450 GPU协议。
申请文件同时警告，公司可能无法实现或维持盈利，预计成本仍将继续上升。

content.v: "We are Mass Effect," the fan group behind a currently 224,000 signature Change.org petition seeking to secure the series' future, has rented out digital billboard space in New York's Times Square to promote the effort.

The group shared a video of the billboard in the wild on X, "The Everything App." Every hour at 35 minutes past the hour, the screen at 1560 Broadway shows a 15-second motion graphic message. Over a planetary vista reminiscent of Mass Effect 1's start screen, we get a distinctive N7 red stripe and the message "Keelah si'yah, #SaveMassEffect" in the series' go-to " Korataki " font. Yes, today is when I too learned that Mass Effect used a commercially-available font called "Korataki" for its logo and in-game text. I kinda want to write all my drafts in it now.

🚨 WE'RE IN TIMES SQUARE!Together with @kalaelizabeth, we've managed to get a #SaveMassEffect billboard up in Times Square, NYC, all day today!📍 1560 Broadway, above the Pelé store (Duffy Square)⏰ 15 seconds every hour at :35HOLD THE LINE! ❤️ https://t.co/wNP9Ak9Vh8 October 26, 2026

"Keelah si'yah" is a phrase from the Quarian language in the games. Continuing today's theme of new discoveries about a series I've spent, like, 1,000 hours playing over 20 years, I learned that this language is called "Khellish." The phrase means "by the homeworld I hope to find one day," not to be confused with "keelah se'lai " or "by the homeworld I hope to see one day." I was more familiar with the latter from the games.

When we checked in on #SaveMassEffect yesterday, it was still at 180,000 signatures , so pretty impressive momentum still. The petition's demands are fairly broad: A commitment of any kind by EA to continue the series in videogame form (not just the Amazon TV series still in development), either internally or by licensing to another party.

I know my ideal solution would be spinning off BioWare, either as an independent (potentially government-supported ) concern, or by selling it to a new corporate owner. The studio's leaked trailer and reported vision for the canceled Mass Effect Universe struck me as both bold (600 years in the future but still tracking choices from the original trilogy ) yet intriguingly specific (a galactic spy thriller ). It reminds me of Joplin, the heist and intrigue-focused original pitch for Dragon Age 4 that was canceled in favor of Anthem.

Out of curiosity, I looked up the cost of a Times Square billboard activation like this. Plug Talk Media lists its single day, 15-second share price as $1,200-$3,500 as a frame of reference. A chunk of change, to be sure, but pretty doable split multiple ways.

content.v: 此前，外媒Eurogamer的编辑Emma Kent为《影之刃零》打出了3星评价，在Metacritic（M站）的换算系统中折算为60分。
《影之刃零》 预售进行中 ！叠加金币至高省40元，每周抽10份免单，还送大作优惠券！
https://img1.gamersky.com/upimg/pic/2026/10/27/small_202610270914109378.jpg
这一分数在玩家群体中引发巨大争议，而随着事态发酵，该评测者在社交媒体上透露，自己因此遭到了极其恶劣的网络暴力。
Emma Kent昨晚在社交媒体上发文，曝光了她因撰写这篇评测而收到的仇恨邮件。她写道：“如果你想知道女性评测者在这里面临着怎样的处境，我已经开始收到让我去死的邮件了……就因为一篇大体上很积极的评测。”她紧接着补充道：“邮件里还说应该强暴我。所以，别告诉我这里面没有性别因素。”
https://img1.gamersky.com/upimg/pic/2026/10/27/small_202610270913473015.png
面对这种极端的网络暴力，有网友对Emma表示了安慰与支持：“这更多地反映了评论者的素质，而不是你或你的评测。他们根本不在乎游戏或评测本身，他们只是不满这篇评测是由一个女人写的。不过平心而论，在我年轻时，3/5依然被认为是个不错的评价，说明游戏优点还是多于缺点的。”
Emma对此回复道：“谢谢！我同意。不幸的是，我觉得人们对M站的均分变得过于执念了，他们只在乎那个数字，而不是评测本身。”
https://img1.gamersky.com/upimg/pic/2026/10/27/small_202610270914195138.jpg
随后，外媒Gamesradar的编辑Scott也发文声援Emma：“很遗憾发生这种事。我今早读了你的评测，认为写得非常出色。这绝对是M站星级换算机制造成的又一个受害者，玩家只盯着那个数字看。”

content.v: 《波斯王子》创作者乔丹·梅克纳肯定了《波斯王子：失落的王冠》的2D银恶城结构，并认为它可能成为新一代玩家接触该系列的起点。这次公开的访谈实际完成于2024年。
https://img.3dmgame.com/uploads/images/news/20261027/1793063562_559887_jpg_r.jpg
梅克纳认为，蒙彼利埃团队选择2D银恶城结构十分聪明。游戏的 奇幻 元素和动画化视觉风格既让人想起系列早期的2D作品，也与《波斯王子：时之砂》形成联系。他此前并非银恶城游戏玩家，《波斯王子：失落的王冠》是他第一款真正投入游玩的此类作品。
https://img.3dmgame.com/uploads/images/news/20261027/1793063565_506665.jpg

https://img.3dmgame.com/uploads/images/news/20261027/1793063567_851484_jpg_r.jpg

游戏采用过去时旁白，不仅借此塑造王子与法拉的关系，也能在玩家死亡时用“事情并非如此”化解叙事矛盾。梅克纳还透露，《波斯王子：武者之心》转向更成熟的分级源于营销要求，并非开发团队最初的主意。

content.v: 索尼正在调查PSN家庭管理功能的一项疑似安全问题。多名用户称，未经授权的陌生账户被添加为自己的“儿童家庭成员”，密码和双重验证似乎未能阻止这一操作，但具体方式及技术原因尚未得到索尼确认。
https://img.3dmgame.com/uploads/images/news/20261027/1793063424_260072_jpg_r.jpg
风险与PlayStation家庭系统的权限设计有关。根据家长控制设置，儿童账户可能游玩账户中的游戏，也可能通过已关联的付款方式在PlayStation Store购买内容。部分用户还担心，陌生账户可能看到姓名等账户及个人资料。
异常账户加入后，用户也难以自行处理。索尼家庭管理帮助页面显示，成人家庭成员可以移除，儿童成员则不能直接从家庭中删除，只有达到相应年龄并升级为成人账户后才能改变身份。三年前的一起类似案例中，陌生儿童账户曾使用用户的信用卡消费；用户可以调整设置阻止后续购买，却无法直接移除该账户。
近期报告主要来自日本用户，但这一问题并非仅在日本出现。调查期间，用户可检查家庭成员列表并继续启用双重验证；若发现陌生账户，应联系PlayStation客服请求处理。目前所谓“双重验证遭绕过”仍来自用户报告，不能视为索尼已经确认的漏洞机制。

如果移除玩家威胁，同一批战利品的获取难度和成就感也会发生变化。作者担心，一旦PvE能够以更低风险提供接近PvPvE玩法的收益，玩家便缺少承担伏击以及损失物资风险的理由，撤离射击玩法的风险回报结构也可能因此削弱。
作者并未主张让PvE奖励失去价值，而是建议明确区分两种体验，例如将PvE战利品上限设为绿色稀有度，让玩家仍能取得实用资源，同时把最稀有、最有价值的装备留给风险更高的远征。具体平衡方式仍应由Embark决定，这项绿色品质上限也只是评论建议，并非开发团队公布的永久模式方案。

items.summary: 微软正寻找合作伙伴共同支持 Arkane Lyon 工作室，以完成《漫威刀锋战士》的后续开发。为了探讨更多解决方案，微软已将为该工作室寻找新买家的期限延长一个月。如果仍未能找到买家，217名员工将面临解雇风险。 微软原本

content.v: 微软正寻找合作伙伴共同支持 Arkane Lyon 工作室，以完成《漫威刀锋战士》的后续开发。为了探讨更多解决方案，微软已将为该工作室寻找新买家的期限延长一个月。如果仍未能找到买家，217名员工将面临解雇风险。
https://image.gcores.com/c42ec4ed51a30c65f800f5f63e63919a-1672-941.webp
微软原本计划在夏季裁员中关闭该工作室，但受限于法国劳动法未能立即执行。7月16日，工作室首次获知这一决定。此前，Xbox新任首席执行官阿莎·夏尔玛公布了针对多家工作室的重组计划，其中 Ninja Theory 被关闭，其余工作室转向独立。
微软发言人向 PC Gamer 表示：“我们在探索方案的同时将协商期延长了一个月，其中包括寻找合作伙伴支持工作室完成后续开发。这是一次有明确期限的延长，我们将在整个过程中保持向职工委员会通报信息。”
https://image.gcores.com/0b427c45bea1596416cb1b1e46e49f0d-399-501.jpg
彭博社记者杰森·施赖埃尔表示：“尽管目前充斥着负面消息，据我了解，仍有多种方案在积极推进以拯救 Arkane Lyon。谈判期间什么都可能发生，但就目前而言，如果工作室被关闭，我会感到意外。”他还指出，根据法国劳动法规定，关闭法国工作室需要支付长期的遣散费。由于成本极其昂贵，微软并不希望承担这笔开销。
工会正在争取将受影响员工调配至微软旗下其他游戏工作室。工会代表指出：“裁员计划必须适应电子游戏市场的现状，目前重新就业的前景非常有限。”代表强调，微软为了节省资金和提高短期投资收益，试图出售一家运营良好的工作室，工会不排除通过法律手段解决纠纷。
《漫威刀锋战士》于2023年12月首次公布预告片。该项目预计在明年年初公开更多细节，并计划于2027年第四季度正式发售。Bethesda 游戏工作室负责人陶德·霍华德表示，自己在今年5月看过项目进展，对 Arkane Lyon 的开发工作表示肯定。

items.title: 曝索尼锁定PS6世代一独占技术！其他厂家不许用
items.summary: 该说法来自播客中的幕后讨论，独占范围与是否成真均无官方确认。

content.v: 据Twisted Voxel报道，“数毛社”Digital Foundry的Richard Leadbetter在近期一期Patreon独家的节目中提到，关于传闻中的PS6机，“有一些幕后讨论称，索尼在其即将推出的移动设备上对掌机用RDNA5拥有某种形式的独占”。这一说法随后经Reddit传播，被多家外媒转述。
https://img1b.gamersky.com/new/content/2026/10/27/cas_auto/small_0_9105550.jpg
需要说明的是，这并非官方消息。索尼至今没有正式公布这款掌机，AMD方面也没有就所谓独占安排作出回应。Leadbetter的表述本身也留有余地——“某种形式的独家”究竟指完全排他，还是优先供货、优先定制之类的安排，目前无法确认。
https://img1b.gamersky.com/new/content/2026/10/27/cas_auto/small_0_9105551.jpg
Twisted Voxel随后推演了这背后的商业逻辑：AMD可能不太愿意把工程资源投向低产量产品的半定制芯片。如果厂商无法承诺足够的订单量，为其单独开发定制芯片的吸引力就会下降。按这一假设，索尼传闻中的掌机可能成为唯一采用RDNA 5专用定制芯片的便携游戏系统，其他设备则可能改用不同图形架构或现有芯片设计。
对掌机玩家来说，这条传闻的分量在于架构差异可能牵动未来的性能表现与游戏适配。报道提到，其他设备可能包括未来的Steam Deck或Xbox掌机，但这些同样只是推测性表述，没有任何一方给出确认。
https://img1b.gamersky.com/new/content/2026/10/27/cas_auto/small_0_9105552.jpg
此前还有报道称，索尼的下一款掌机可能采用六核CPU，包含四个Zen 6核心和两个Zen 6低功耗核心，一份官方Linux内核补丁被认为为这些早先说法增添了可信度，但它并未确认传闻中设备的完整规格。芯片独占的说法与这些规格爆料是否互相印证，目前仍缺乏直接证据。

items.title: 50 个最常玩的 Steam Next Fest 演示包括 7 款增量游戏、4 款 AI 披露以及只有 1 个 haystack slop 实例
items.summary: Ten years ago, this list would have shocked most PC gamers.

content.v: Last week's Steam Next Fest had over 8,000 demos; now Valve has revealed the 50 most-played among them. The results aren't surprising: there's lots of friendsloppy casual co-op, incremental games continue to be popular, and players have by-and-large rejected games with overt generative AI use, with only four of the games among the 50 declaring AI use in development.
Here are some other factoids:
Among all 50 of these games, the only entry published by a traditional "blockbuster" publisher was Tropico 7, a Ubisoft affair [Oops, it's actually a Kalypso Media affair].
Teach My Little Sister How To Drive was one of the four games with AI disclosures. It leans heavily on an LLM-powered NPC which apparently cost its developer over $1,000 a day .

I'm not super surprised by the list, which you can find here , and which is topped by 1-6 player "asymmetric party game" Worst Class Ever . I'm not surprised because it really does capture the zeitgeist, but it's nevertheless pretty eye-opening when you compare it to the kinds of games that dominated the event only five years ago. For example, this Reddit thread lists highlights like Norco, Death Trash, Sable, Unpacking and The Inheritance of Crimson Manor, all of which people still talk about and play (though I am still waiting for Death Trash to enter 1.0).

It's hard not to see the outsize influence of Roblox and UGC in general on this list, which can sometimes be unappreciated by people who like to pay for games on Steam and read about them on PC Gamer. It's possible that the kids who were reared on cheap smartphone software are responsible for the surge in freewheeling online co-op games with simple graphics, but whatever the case, 2026 feels very, very different to 2021.

items.summary: Dead by Daylight developer Behaviour Interactive has responded after confirming Chucky would be removed from s

content.v: https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2026/10/26/chucky-dead-by-daylight-1793058562712.png

Dead by Daylight developer Behaviour Interactive has responded after confirming Chucky would be removed from stores last week, explaining that horror icons will "continue to have an open invitation to join (or rejoin)."

There was a bit of confusion amongst fans when the studio behind the hit asymmetrical horror game announced Chucky as the latest icon to leave its roster . Following the removal of Pinhead last year and Michael Myers just months ago, fans were sad to see another Killer exit stores so soon.

However, it's ultimately not up to Behaviour when it comes to the date some franchises may depart. In a statement sent to IGN, Behaviour said that, while its "goal is always to keep licenses" in Dead by Daylight forever, that can't always be the case. That's why, "despite our best efforts," Chucky and others have left and could continue to leave in the future.

No one wants to see Dead by Daylight's staggering roster of Killers and Survivors shrink for any reason, especially when Behaviour has consistently delivered variety in the decade since its launch . Unfortunately, that's what will happen come November 24, 2026, when the Chucky Chapter is made unavailable to purchase.

The upside, as Behaviour made clear in last week's announcement, is that anyone who purchases the possessed killer doll and any of his accompanying cosmetics will have the freedom to use them beyond the cutoff date. It means that, while Chucky may show up in fewer lobbies over time, he'll never truly be gone.

It's something Behaviour made sure to reiterate in its statement to IGN, reassuring fans that "Dead by Daylight will always be gaming's House of Horror." This means that, even when licenses expire, the Child's Play , Halloween, and Hellraiser franchises will always have the same invitation to enter the Fog that newcomers have. You can see the studio's full statement on Chucky's exit below.

"As with all live service games, players can expect regular updates, new content, and occasional changes over time," Behaviour said. "Our goal is always to keep licenses in our game forever. When they have to go away, it's because - despite our best efforts - it wasn't possible to retain them.

"We want to reassure our community that Chucky will remain part of the Dead by Daylight experience for existing owners. Players who already own The Good Guy, his perks, or any associated cosmetics will still be able to use that content after November 24, 2026.
"Dead by Daylight will always be gaming's House of Horror, and horror icons will continue to have an open invitation to join (or rejoin) us in the Fog."

It'll be painful to see one of Dead by Daylight's more unique Killers leave the Fog, but a return is definitely not off the table. One of the more famous examples of an IP leaving and eventually coming back was Stranger Things and its playable Demogorgon, which was removed from stores in November 2021 before being added back in November 2023.

For now, there's no telling when Chucky and Child's Play may return. Meanwhile, we recently found out that Terrifier's Art the Clown would enter the fray starting next month. Friday the 13th's Jason was added in June. For more, you can check out everything Behaviour announced during its 10th Anniversary Broadcast over the summer.

The Ukiyo Game Bar in Tokyo is going viral for its unique guest experience that lets customers play Buckshot Roulette in real life… well, sort of.

First announced on October 9, guests can make their reservations to play a game of Buckshot Roulette until November 9, 2026. Of course, this isn’t actual Russian Roulette (which would be extremely dangerous, not to mention wildly illegal), but instead a fun recreation of the viral indie game with non-lethal mechanics.

As shown in a tweet posted by the bar and photos shared by guests, hosts will don a mask of the dealer’s terrifying face and wield a prop shotgun as players gather round the roulette table with their drinks in tow.

Speaking of drinks, Ukiyo Game Bar also has a few themed cocktails on offer, one of which is themed after the hit indie game Arctic Eggs . Made in collaboration with the game’s developer, The Water Museum, this delightful drink even features a gummy in the shape of a fried egg. (These gummies aren’t actually available in Japan; an American staff member shipped 2 kilos worth of them in from the States.)
Photos of the Buckshot Roulette experience quickly went viral on social media, leaving fans with severe FOMO and scrambling to make travel plans.

In Buckshot Roulette, players sign a waiver and engage in a version of Russian Roulette with a Shotgun against a mysterious and terrifying opponent. There’s more to it than pulling the trigger and hoping you don’t meet a grisly end; there are a variety of items on offer that players can use to their advantage and tip the odds in their favor with the goal of surviving — and making off with a major cash prize.

items.summary: If last week's mysterious Mass Effect: Universe trailer leak wasn't painful enough for you in the wake of BioW

content.v: If last week's mysterious Mass Effect: Universe trailer leak wasn't painful enough for you in the wake of BioWare's sudden closure , we've gotten yet another taste of The Game That Could Have Been, this time courtesy of award-winning video game composer Austin Wintory.

Known for his beautiful and haunting soundtracks for games like Flow, Journey, ABZÛ , Aliens: Fireteam Elite, Sword of The Sea , John Wick Hex, and Hades II , Wintory was also evidently working on the Mass Effect: Universe soundtrack. From the sounds of things, EA and the now-defunct BioWare were considering having Wintory produce the game's OST. And thanks to Wintory, we at least know what the game might have sounded like.

"Mass Effect was my ultimate white whale, my all-time dream project," Wintory wrote in a post on Bluesky . "For the last couple years I'd been in discussion with BioWare & EA to take on the project, and as part of that, I wrote close to 20 minutes of music to explore where the franchise can go next. May as well share it!"
Wintory shared the music alongside an image that reads, "Mass Effect: Universe, the music that might have been."

"So here you go," Wintory added in a follow-up post linking to a YouTube upload of the test-run tracks. "Thank you again to my friends at both BioWare and EA. To even dream in your sandbox was a privilege."

The video features 20 minutes of Wintory's experimental score, featuring seven unique tracks and one remix. Text displayed within the video itself also reveals more about the nature of Wintory's talks with EA and BioWare, along with his inspiration for the soundtrack.

"In 2007, when the credits rolled on my first playthrough of Mass Effect, I remember calling a friend and saying, 'I can't believe I already know this will be among my favorite all-time games.' Usually, it takes the passage of time before we can be so sure something truly belongs to the ages, but in this case, the confidence was instantaneous," Wintory wrote. "This trilogy is my most-cherished gaming experience of my lifetime, and as a professional composer, represented my most sought-after 'White Whale.' For me, there is no greater dream project to be part of."

According to Wintory, nothing had been finalized yet, but both EA and BioWare seemed eager to get him on board. So Wintory, in all his love for the franchise, cooked up a little surprise for the Mass Effect: Universe team.

"For the past several years, I'd been in dialogue with people both at BioWare and EA to potentially jump into Mass Effect 5," Wintory explained. "As part of those conversations, I decided to surprise the team by writing/recording a giant love letter to the franchise, with my idea of where it can go next. When I wrote this (in 2025), I knew nothing of what they were planning, so this was a bit narratively speculative. The concept was a direct homage to Jack Wall and Sam Hulick's incredible work on the first game, while leaning even harder on true analog synths, and a more complex integration of the orchestra (almost akin to the hybrid nature of The Matrix)."
While it seems that Mass Effect: Universe will never see the light of day, at least we have the beautiful soundtrack-that-could-have been, for what looked to be an equally beautiful game.

items.summary: Blizzard dropped a final balance pass for each playable race's unique abilities.

content.v: The World of Warcraft: Forever min-maxers have been arguing about the pros and cons of each playable race since the throwback MMO was announced. It isn't enough to just pick whoever looks cool for some people. They need to know how the math works out so they don't spend a hundred hours leveling a character who will do 3% less damage than the others.

Admittedly, WoW: Forever will be stuck in an era where unique racial abilities and traits mattered a lot more than they do in the modern version of the MMO. Some of them directly synergize with certain classes and others just make your life a lot easier for what will be a long journey. This is probably why Blizzard is still tweaking them a week from launch day.

Despite trying to balance them evenly before, Blizzard is doubling down on some racials having clear advantages for certain classes over others. You can see how this looks in today's patch notes , but you won't be able to test anything out until the WoW: Forever goes live next week.

Most of the changes fit that ethos: orcs, for example, won't have an increased critical strike chance but increased pet damage for warlocks and hunters. The skyborne, the new blue elves, had their absurdly powerful Read Leyline ability that makes them regenerate health and mana faster than anyone else cut in half. It's still good, but not broken good.
And then there are the tauren, the bipedal bovines who have been in WoW since the beginning, who have apparently discovered nitrous oxide.

Blizzard has blessed the tauren with a passive that increases your movement speed the longer you stay in motion. Plainsrunning was already strong as a way to move 30% faster than everyone else in the game, but the new patch doubles it to 60%. With enough time to gain speed, tauren will be as fast as the mounts you have to pay hundreds of gold for.

I kind of admire how much Blizzard is leaning into this idea, even if it costs tauren some minor damage buffs. There's a long-running joke among WoW players that playing a tauren makes you move slower. This is because they're so huge that their run animation just looks like they're moving in slow-motion compared to the rest of the cast. Now, the joke's on us, I guess.

Setting aside taurens growing wheels, messing with racial abilities this close to launch is brave. Blizzard intends to regularly balance WoW: Forever, but this is the kind of foundational stuff it won't be able to touch without pissing a ton of people off. Even if most people probably won't have the tier lists open for the best race/class combinations, they will still inevitably influence what kind of meta materializes for high-end PvP and raiding.

items.summary: World of Warcraft: Forever's release is just around the corner, but developer Blizzard is making one final pas

content.v: World of Warcraft: Forever's release is just around the corner, but developer Blizzard is making one final pass at the game's racial abilities before launch in response to beta feedback.

In a forum post , WoW community manager Kaivax posted a list of significant changes to many of each race's unique abilities that players expressed concerns about during Forever's beta. Those changes include tweaks to tauren, humans, orcs, dwarves, and Skyborne elves.

"In taking a final pass on these, we've prioritized racial identity, which means that some races will naturally be slightly more effective than others at certain combat roles," Blizzard said. "In some places where we had replaced role or class-focused racials with generic ones, we're rolling those changes back."

The exception to that mindset is weapon-specialization abilities, Blizzard said, which existed for humans and orcs both in WoW Classic and early on in Forever's beta and made each race more effective with specific types of weapons.

"While those have a strong fantasy component to them, it is not healthy in the long run for future raid and dungeon loot tables to be evaluated through the lens of 'required' weapon types," Blizzard said. "At the same time, we're doing a tuning pass on some of the remaining passive bonuses to help ensure that they aren't skewing outcomes in a way that limits player preferences."

Humans, widely viewed by the community as one of the most "optimal" races to pick thanks to their powerful passive abilities, have lost some of their power in combat. Ruthless now only grants 1% critical strike chance instead of 2%. In exchange, their Human Spirit passive has been buffed from 5% to 10%.

Tauren have seen some significant changes, with massive buffs to their unique Plainsrunning ability but a loss to some of their combat effectiveness. Plainsrunning will now grant 2% movement speed per stack up to a max of 60% increased movement speed, at the price of no longer increasing mounted movement speed and the loss of hit chance and crit damage from their Endurance passive.

Orcs have seen their 1% crit chance removed and replaced with an earlier passive, Command. Now, orcs will deal 5% increased Warlock and Hunter pet damage. Dwarves have had their critical damage passive removed, instead replaced with a 1% chance to hit with attacks and spells.

Last but not least, Forever's newest race, Skyborne elves, have seen some major changes. Their haste bonus from Wind-Blessed has been reduced to 2% from 3%. They also now benefit more from using their Skysight and Read Leyline abilities at elemental convergence or leyline sites, with stronger effects that persist through death.

It's just the latest (and sounds like the last, at least for a while) batch of changes to Forever's various races . Blizzard said these changes, a little over a week before Forever's launch, were to address feedback players had during the beta about some abilities feeling "too generic," while others were "objectively stronger than others." You can read the full racial ablity changes below.

Blizzard looks to be making plenty of changes to Forever in the last stretch before release. It announced last week that it will be getting a new PvP-server option after all, and that the MMORPG's controversial layering system will see improvements in time for launch. WoW: Forever arrives November 4.

content.v: 《 生化奇兵 》电影改编项目仍在推进。导演弗朗西斯·劳伦斯表示，项目已经“接近”向现实迈进一步，但Netflix近期的管理层变动也带来了新的不确定性。
https://img.3dmgame.com/uploads/images/news/20261027/1793052839_798326_jpg_r.jpg
Netflix于2022年宣布推进这部电影，之后确定由劳伦斯执导。不过，劳伦斯手中还有《红色崛起》改编等多个项目，目前无法保证《生化奇兵》会成为他下一部执导的影片。制片人Roy Lee此前确认，电影将以初代游戏而非续作为改编基础。
劳伦斯认为，改编的核心难题是将游戏依靠玩家参与形成的叙事转化为传统电影。原作主角杰克近乎沉默，玩家探索海底城市销魂城时，会相信自己正在主动选择，而自由意志、选择错觉又与关键反转紧密相连。电影需要重新塑造主角，观众旁观他人作出选择时，原有冲击力也可能减弱。
好莱坞过去近二十年曾多次尝试改编《生化奇兵》。环球影业2008年取得版权后，戈尔·维宾斯基与编剧约翰·洛根一度将R级版本推进至距离开拍仅数周的阶段，最终因预算问题搁浅。吉尔莫·德尔·托罗也曾指出，游戏中的解谜、信息拼合和受引导选择等体验很难直接移植到电影中。当前版本尚未正式开机，项目仍处于开发阶段。

https://img.3dmgame.com/uploads/images/news/20261027/1793052746_173725_jpg_r.jpg
这些角色还会观察玩家如何战斗、入侵和制作物品，也会留意玩家对待另外两名角色的方式，并根据这些行为作出回应。因此，不同选择带来的变化可能不只出现在结局，还会贯穿人物关系、对白、机制和故事进程。
这一方向与《生化奇兵》形成对照。后者通过质体、武器和环境互动提供了较高的战斗自由度，但主线中的有限叙事控制权本身也是剧情揭示与主题表达的一部分，不能简单归为设计缺陷。《犹大》则似乎准备进一步扩大玩家对叙事过程的影响。
Levine曾以《中土世界：暗影魔多》的宿敌系统说明动态关系带来的启发，并将《犹大》漫长的开发周期归因于复杂的“叙事乐高”系统。这套设计能否让关系与故事真正持续响应玩家选择，仍需以成品表现为准。

items.summary: Don't blame this one on GTA 6: The developers say incorporating feedback on Emberville's demo is taking longer

content.v: Literally one day before it was set to launch into early access, the pixel art action RPG Emberville has been delayed so the development team can incorporate feedback from the game's recent Steam Next Fest demo. Instead of rolling out on October 27 as planned, Emberville is now set to launch on January 7.

"Many of you have played our Steam Next Fest demo and shared your feedback. This means a great deal to us, and we immediately started planning more improvements," developer Cygnus Cross wrote in a Steam update . "However, some of the improvements we want to make are systems changes that can't be done quickly. Reworking bow combat, for example, would take more time than we had prior to our Early Access release even though the team is working around the clock.
"After carefully considering our options, we have decided to move the release date and include some essential improvements in the Early Access launch build."

The last minute delay is particularly surprising given that Cygnus Cross reaffirmed the October 27 release just a week ago, with a " what to expect " post for potential players. That included information on Emberville's planned first early access update, which was meant to include the final boss of the first biome, controller support improvements, additional languages, and more, all within a month after the game's launch.

There's no overlooking the looming specter of Grand Theft Auto 6 , which launches for consoles on November 19—an arrival that's caused no small amount of turmoil for other game releases in its proximity.

Frankly, though, I'm not sure how much crossover there would be between the GTA 6 and Emberville audiences, and Cygnus Cross made no mention of it in its delay announcement: The studio said only that its goal "is to deliver an experience that shows what makes the game distinctive, establishes its core gameplay, and offers a compelling glimpse of how the game will grow throughout Early Access."
For those who want to see what Emberville has to offer in its current state, the Emberville demo remains available on Steam .

items.title: 《太平间助理》制作者推出的一款免费“微型”恐怖游戏基本上就相当于《法律与秩序》中的一集
items.summary: Playable Archive is free, and it's very good.

content.v: Halloween is almost upon us, and if you're looking for some suitably spooky videogame fun then allow me to direct your attention to Playable Archive , a free "micro psychological horror experience" from Darkstone Digital, the solo studio behind The Mortuary Assistant.

As you might expect, given the title, Playable Archive bears a number of similarities to PT, the 2014 "playable teaser" for a cancelled game in the Silent Hill series. It takes place (almost) entirely within a single home, the situation starts slow and escalates quickly, and it's the product of a game that was ultimately cancelled and will never see the light of day.

"Releasing Playable Archive is really exciting, and it feels like some form of personal healing," Darkstone Digital owner Brian Clarke said. "After working for so long on something I cared so much about, it felt wrong to leave it sitting on the shelf like some cursed item.

"Although the full-scale game this demo was built for will never see the light of day and many pieces of it had to be left on the cutting room floor, I feel like it’s important to honor what was built. Immortalizing the project's memory with Playable Archive is my way of doing that while offering something new from me for horror fans this Halloween as I get to work on new projects."
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/N5WXFQSCttV6Am7CopwTzd-1920-80.png
This article is brought to you by No More Room in Hell 2 .

I took Playable Archive for a spin, and it is creepy. I'm keeping things vague to avoid spoilers, but it's a found-footage game about a young couple who purchase a dilapidated home and set about renovating it, leading to an unfortunate discovery and rapidly deteriorating circumstances. A big mid-game twist elicited a genuine wtf from me, and things went downhill even more quickly from there. The more I learned the worse I felt, and the more I wanted to know: What the hell is really going on here?

I had a similar meta-feeling about the demo itself, which made me wonder: Is this slice of a never-to-be-released game actually part of a feeling-out process, to see if maybe the game it came from should be released? So I asked—and the answer came back a firm 'no.'

"I loved the project, but I spent such time and effort on it that it would simply be too much to try to toil away on it again for who knows how long," Clarke told me. "I have no desire to revisit it at this point other than for inspiration. From the very beginning it was designed with Paranormal Activity in mind, so I'd rather spend my efforts creating something new than trying to force something new from an existing project."

Hunter Bond, director of publisher DreadXP, said effectively the same thing: "Brian was still haunted by the game he worked on for years not being publicly playable in any form. I asked if he agreed that it would both be a cool and amusing thing to do to just release it into the wild for free so that people could experience it. We feel good about the choice we made to support Brian and cancel it when he wasn't going to be given enough time to get it to the level it deserved. We all hope people enjoy it, but I wouldn't ask him to retread this ground. Instead I'm excited to see what he works on next now that he can have some closure with this."

Playable Archive doesn't have a save function, which should be fine for most people—it's a "micro" horror game, remember, with an estimated running time of just 30-60 minutes. I actually hit a snag near the end of that window, which I unfortunately didn't have time to figure out because I had to work. (Life is so unfair.) But it's interesting enough that I'm going to jump back into it tonight and take it all the way through to whatever end awaits: I know the mystery won't be resolved, but it's enough fun, in the horror game sense of the word, that I want to get as far with it as I can anyway.

Playable Archive is available now on Steam , and in case you didn't see it the first time—that happens sometimes, in horror games—it's free. Once you've got it wrapped up, be sure to check out our Halloween guide of other games to play, shows to watch, and costumes to wear to properly celebrate this year's spooky season.

items.title: GTA 6 导致游戏发布日期请假请求激增 17%
items.summary: GTA 6's release has led to as much as a 17% increase in time-off requests, according to a new report.

content.v: https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2026/09/17/gta-6-soundtrack-1789662158949.jpg
GTA 6's release has led to as much as a 17% increase in time-off requests, according to a new report.

As reported by Money.com , new data from HR software company BambooHR revealed that there has been a notable spike in time-off requests for November 19. BambooHR revealed that there has been an increase between 9% to 17% on November 19, compared to normal requests for the third Thursday in November. While we aren't sure if every single person is taking that day off to play GTA 6, it stands to reason that this is what the bulk of these requests are for.

Economists have estimated a $1 billion loss in productivity in the United States due to GTA 6's release. While we'll just have to wait and see what kind of impact the game has on the world, it is clear that this is a massive event. There's a high level of anticipation for GTA 6, and it is expected to have one of the biggest entertainment launches of all time, if not the biggest.

Rockstar has also been spending a ton of money to get the word out with extravagant marketing; it spent $975,000 to install a massive neon pink sign on top of the Miami Heat's arena, after all. The developer also covered the city with in-universe ads for brands in the game, along with more traditional banners featuring the game's key art. Fans can even eat at a real life version of Burger Shot , a fast food chain in the GTA universe, if they live in Miami.

There will also be an unprecedented NBA game between the Miami Heat and the Milwaukee Bucks on November 18, which will turn the Heat into the Vice City Heat . They will play with GTA 6-themed jerseys on a never-before-seen Vice City court. It should be quite the spectacle, and serve as an effective final marketing beat for the game.
GTA 6 will release on November 19 for PS5 and Xbox Series X|S. A PC port is also rumored for early 2027.

items.title: 我最喜欢的 2020 年代 RPG 游戏之一的开发商之所以这么做，是因为 BioWare：“博德之门 1 是我真正喜欢的第一款游戏”
items.summary: It's a hard one to beat.

content.v: As part of our ongoing coverage and commemoration of the closure of BioWare, we've been reaching out to RPG developers to hear what the studio meant to them. Lead SEO editor Lauren Morton got in touch with 16 devs who owe their careers to the legendary RPG studio , and today I can share the words of another, Skald: Against the Black Priory lead developer Anders Lauridsen.

I had a similar experience with BioWare RPGs as a substitute for tabletop growing up, lacking friends who were interested in the hobby until well into adulthood, and I'll wager that's not an uncommon experience.

Hearing Lauridsen say there's a lot of BioWare DNA in Skald made me smile. The game's art recalls those clunkier RPGs the developer initially bounced off, but its mechanics and combat are Baldur's Gate and Fallout to the core. I also gotta say I feel less bad about my own lack of facility with earlier generations of CRPG after hearing that a developer like Lauridsen struggled with them at first.

His enthusiasm is a heartening reminder that BioWare's legacy is more durable than EA's quarterly profits or private equity predation: The things we love about those games have dispersed into RPGs all over the world, and Skald is a perfect example of that.

It has the tight, low-level focus of the original Baldur's Gate, but with a shocking inflection of cosmic horror , plus Larianesque reactive systems I never would have expected from a pixel art game⁠—Larian's own Swen Vincke is a fan of Skald himself . It's $15 on Steam and GOG (half-off at the latter at the time of writing), and I reviewed it on Steam Deck , where it runs like a dream.

items.title: 资深游戏作曲家在为《质量效应 5》配乐的谈话中分享了他为该项目创作的 20 分钟音乐：“在沙盒中做梦都是一种荣幸”
items.summary: We're so back / It's so over / We were so robbed.

content.v: Composer Austin Wintory (Journey, Stray Gods, Assassin's Creed: Syndicate) just shared 20 minutes of music he wrote as a sort of audition/starting point for the score of Mass Effect 5, aka. Mass Effect: Universe. According to Wintory, he had been in "serious conversation" with BioWare and EA to provide the game's soundtrack.

To be clear: This was not music that was 100% slated to appear in the game, but it sounds like Wintory was on the shortest of shortlists for the job. The effective EP is presented as "My Mass Effect 5 early musical drafts" and "Mass Effect: Universe, the music that might have been."

Wintory wrote that he wanted to "surprise [EA and BioWare] with an elaborate production" in 2025, and that the music was recorded with "synths, vocals, and a large orchestra here in LA." Noting that he didn't have story details for the in-development game, Wintory came up with speculative themes and track titles based on the series' past.

And I really don't know how to process that this thing whips ass . Wintory had a killer vision with the project: "My suggestion was to treat the original game's masterful Jack Wall / Sam Hulick score as a starting point," he wrote, "And to build on it from there with deeper use of physical, analog synths and a more tightly interwoven use of the orchestra. But a love letter first and foremost."

God damn it . Mass Effect had great music throughout the series, but ME1's more synth-heavy approach has always been my favorite. Wintory still makes great use of the orchestra, but the synths are back , baby. Balance has been restored. This stuff gave me chills.

Both versions of main theme candidate "The Legacy of Shepard" are favorites for me, but I'd also like to shout out the more up-tempo, combat-ready "Hold the Line." Wintory was onto something here, and it also clearly meant a great deal to the composer. Wintory described this as a "dream project" and "white whale." I wish we could have heard the whole OST.

items.summary: Forbidden Solitaire's The Discarded DLC is here and those cards aren't going to play themselves.

content.v: The first new card I found in Forbidden Solitaire's new DLC The Discarded gave me the power to throw a card like a knife at whatever horror was trying to kill me. Although nothing warranted such a desperate move, I fear it won't be long before I find myself out of options now that I've seen the devilish new tricks the developers have dealt in the DLC's first hour.

I'm lucky I just spent the last week playing through the base game because The Discarded offers no help: From the moment you double click the DLC executable on the game's '90s-inspired PC interface, you're on your own. It's not quite enough to understand how to play solitaire; you need to know how to play Forbidden Solitaire , a haunted version of the classic card game where you must change your approach based on the modified cards the developers throw at you.

Some cards might be locked away until you play the right suits. Others might be surrounded by bones, requiring them to be played twice before leaving the board. Your deck will run out quickly if you don't strategize around these factors and try to knock off as many cards as you can in one turn.

Thankfully, you can cheat… by jamming gems into your flesh. The eyeball in the wall that compels you to mutilate your hand for power is back. This time, you can even sear glyphs into your skin, too. Each unholy decoration gives you bonuses that can help tilt the balance in your favor, like an increased chance to deal extra damage during combat—oh yeah, there's combat .
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/M8EgZhVB2JeBqxXcgYm3M6-1920-80.png
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/rPyqqCn5p4qDBnZ3jNczK6-1920-80.png
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/HKKvFxYCsnuQ4f5hzhDnH6-1920-80.png
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/aVuT5Yp9UXx6hFmRswzKK6-1920-80.png

Right away, The Discarded's enemies don't play around. In the original game, you're taught to pay close attention to whatever horrible thing a monster plans to do once you finish your turn. This can be simply an attack that drains your health or a variety of curses that warp the cards. The beast at the start of the DLC can block you from playing cards by covering them in wet paint, and later you have to deal with marbled cards that don't contribute to your combos—and thus your damage.

I never knew solitaire could have so much depth until I played Forbidden Solitaire, and The Discarded sprinkles even more challenges that change your approach to what is otherwise a pretty straightforward game.

It also helps that there's an entire mystery to unravel as you go. You play the new DLC as Robyn Cierra, a character digging through Forbidden Solitaire, the in-universe 1995 CD-ROM game, in search of their sister. There's another character sending you texts with images and fuzzy FMV clips that detail all the bizarre events surrounding the development of the game, back in the early '90s. And if it's like the base game's story, I don't expect things to stay relatively normal for long.

Forbidden Solitaire is easily one of the best indie card games I've played since Inscryption and The Discarded DLC feels like a spooky encore. If you missed it, I recommend spending the two to three hours it takes to finish the base game first. That way you're prepared for whatever horrors await in the DLC's 30 new levels.
Forbidden Solitaire is currently $11.51, a few bucks off of its normal $16 price for the next week, and you can grab The Discarded DLC for $8.

items.title: 沃尔特·科尼格（Walter Koenig），《星际迷航》的帕维尔·契诃夫（Pavel Chekhov）去世
items.summary: Koenig gained fame as the Russian navigator of the USS Enterprise in the original Star Trek television series,

content.v: A Variety report says that Walter Koenig, known to the world as Star Trek's Russian hothead Pavel Chekhov, has died.

Koenig's big break in show biz came in 1967, when he was cast as Chekhov in the second season of the original Star Trek series. He portrayed the character until the show's cancellation, and then through seven feature films; he had a particularly memorable scene in Star Trek 2: The Wrath of Khan, when a Ceti eel burrowed its way into his brain.
Even now, it's pretty gnarly.

The downside of that early-career fame is that Koenig was typecast, and acting roles following the end of the Star Trek series were sparse. He turned to screenwriting through the 1970s; ironically, while the character of Chekhov was not included in the Star Trek animated series that ran for two seasons after the live-action show was cancelled, he wrote the script for an animated series episode called The Infinite Vulcan, making him the first member of the cast to write an episode for the Star Trek franchise.

But Koenig also played very much against type in at least one memorable role: Alfred Bester, a powerful Psi Corps officer in Babylon 5. Where Chekhov was brash, good-hearted, and a little naive, Bester was a charismatic, stone-cold villain with a talent for manipulation and complete indifference to human life. He was the sort of character who was born to chew scenery, but Koenig took a more understated approach that imbued Bester with real menace. It was a good bit of casting.

Koenig also had a handful of videogame credits to his name, all but one for Star Trek games—the exception being something called Stretch Armstrong: The Breakout, an "interactive movie" created for Netflix in 2018.

My heart is heavy. Walter Koenig, our Ensign Pavel Chekov, passed away early today.Walter and I met on the bridge of the Enterprise in the 1960s, and we stayed friends for nearly six decades. When Brad and I married in 2008, Walter stood beside us as our best man.

"My heart is heavy. Walter Koenig, our Ensign Pavel Chekov, passed away early today," George Takei, who played Koenig's helm partner Hikaru Sulu, wrote on Bluesky. "Walter and I met on the bridge of the Enterprise in the 1960s, and we stayed friends for nearly six decades. When Brad and I married in 2008, Walter stood beside us as our best man.

"Just last month, on Sept. 14, he turned 90, on the same day Brad and I celebrated our 18th wedding anniversary. I will always treasure that he and I shared that date. Walter was more than Chekov. He was a writer, a teacher, a thoughtful man, and a loyal friend. To the fans who loved him for so many years, thank you. He loved you too. Rest well, my dear friend. Keep navigating a steady course."
Variety says Koenig died of natural causes. He was 90.

In The Regreening, you're revitalizing a post-apocalyptic landscape, replanting flora, and designing environments for animals to return to while making friends with godlike animal spirits. It's almost as much a tiny city-builder as a farm sim.

items.summary: The canceled movie spinoff is getting a new lease of life as Playable Archive, released today for free on Stea

content.v: https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2026/10/26/1-1793043605770.jpg

Every horror fan knows the rule: Just when you think the monster is dead, they always come back. The game Paranormal Activity: Threshold is no exception, with the canceled movie spinoff getting a new lease on life as Playable Archive, which is released today, for free, on Steam.

It's your classic tale of a young couple simply trying to do some renovations on their home and ending up paying the price for tampering with a strange object they came across during their remodel. The story is told through found footage and ticks all the spooky boxes with rituals, strange symbols, and shaky camera footage with an ominous entity just out of shot.

The original Paranormal Activity project was killed earlier this year by Paramount , but developer Brian Clarke, who made the jump-scare joy The Mortuary Assistant, worked with publisher DreadXP to resurrect a new version of the game available to horror fans.

"I have to admit, I was feeling burnt out, and I imagined the project would simply sit on a shelf forever. A forgotten relic of development that sat in darkness while I built up a plan for a new project," Clarke said in a Steam post. "DreadXP reached out to me and floated the idea of maybe releasing what I had. It felt like a good way of laying the project to rest instead of remaining a lingering ghost. So, I worked to adjust the project where needed and polished up the edges to release the work I had done. I’m sad to say that a good deal of work was still left on the cutting room floor, but I’m proud of what I am able to share and that it is going to see the light of day in some form."
The game has no save system and needs to be played in one sitting, according to the Steam listing, so be prepared to lock in.
If you're sad about the Paranormal Activity part of it, don't worry; you only have to wait until next year for a new Paranormal Activity movie from James Wan.

items.summary: Diablo 4's War Plans system is getting a major upgrade in Season 16, giving players even more control over the

content.v: Diablo 4's War Plans system is getting a major upgrade in Season 16, giving players even more control over their endgame activities and rewards.

Developer Blizzard introduced War Plans earlier this year as part of the game's second (and last) expansion , Lord of Hatred. It's an endgame system where players can essentially create a playlist of endgame activities, along the way ranking up those activities via a skill tree to make them even more rewarding.

It was a welcome addition, but unfortunately only gave players minimal control over what activities would appear as part of their plans. Players could also only reroll their War Plans a limited number of times, meaning if you didn't like a particular activity, oftentimes you were stuck having to do it.

All of that looks to be changing in Season 16 with the addition of a new meta-progression system called War Plans Tactics. By completing War Plan activities, players will be able to invest points into the tactics tree to make it so certain activities are more likely to appear and specific types of rewards will drop. How players reroll their War Plans is also changing, with a new currency called Marks of Wisdom that will cap at 20 and should let players reroll their plans more often.

As detailed by Blizzard in a blog post ahead of the season arriving on the Diablo 4 public test realm October 27, players will be able to assign up to three points into each endgame activity and up to three points into different types of rewards.

"Earn points from completing War Plans activities, then invest these points into nodes to increase the chance of preferred activities or rewards appearing," Blizzard said. "This allows you to tailor your War Plans more closely with both your goals and playstyle."
https://www.gamespot.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/Diablo-4-S16-War-Plans-Tactics.jpg?w=636

Putting at least one point into Helltides or Nightmare dungeons also grants the choice of increased chances for Greater Helltides and Escalation Nightmare dungeons, respectively. On the reward side, players will be able to make it so they are more likely to earn armor, weapons, jewelry, Obducite, salvage, gems, gold, activity keys, Horadric Cube materials, or Talisman items from activities.

The new tactics system isn't the only change coming to War Plans. A new seasonal War Plans tree, Tyrael's Boons, will also be coming with Season 16. There will be four Tyrael's Boons' paths to invest points into, with Blizzard stating players will be able to choose up to four of the six nodes within each path. Those four paths are:

The changes to War Plans look to be the biggest features coming as part of Season 16, but there will additionally be a new type of gear to acquire, Horadric legendaries. These special legendaries will synergize with specific Talisman charms, with Horadric legendary jewelry items even counting for Talisman set bonuses. That should open the door to all kinds of new set and charm combinations that are sure to result in some wild new endgame builds.

Diablo 4 Season 16 will be playable on the PTR until November 3, with the full season set to launch December 1. Though Diablo 4 won't be getting additional expansions, it will get a new class, the Amazon , in the first half of next year.

As for what's next for the franchise, Diablo 5 is slated to arrive in 2029 . Blizzard has already revealed three of the game's playable classes and promised it will have more classes at launch than any previous Diablo game.

items.summary: The Witcher was developed on BioWare's Aurora engine, but the Dragon Age studio did more than just share its t

content.v: Today, October 26, is the 19 th anniversary of The Witcher, the groundbreaking RPG that introduced Geralt, and CD Projekt, to the world. To mark the moment, CD Projekt took to social to pay tribute to friends who made it all possible: BioWare.

CD Projekt joint CEO Michał Nowakowski spoke warmly of BioWare last week in the immediate aftermath of the studio's shocking closure , crediting it as "a massive part of CDPR history." The Witcher was built on BioWare's Aurora engine, which it created for Neverwinter Nights, but BioWare did more than just share technology: It also worked to help bring the upstart Polish RPG to much wider attention.

"19 years ago, an ambitious dream to bring an iconic book series into the world of video games came to life with the release of The Witcher. It was the start of an unforgettable path, which wouldn't have been possible without our friends at BioWare," CD Projekt wrote.

"From lending us their Aurora Engine and sharing their knowledge, to giving us a spot at their booth at E3, their support helped turn our vision into Geralt’s first interactive adventure. Thank you to everyone who has walked the Path with us from the very beginning. Happy 19th anniversary, witchers!"

19 years ago, an ambitious dream to bring an iconic book series into the world of video games came to life with the release of The Witcher.It was the start of an unforgettable path, which wouldn't have been possible without our friends at BioWare.

From lending us their Aurora Engine and sharing their knowledge, to giving us a spot at their booth at E3, their support helped turn our vision into Geralt’s first interactive adventure.Thank you to everyone who has walked the Path with us from the very beginning.Happy 19th anniversary, witchers!

The first Witcher game, released in 2007 as a PC exclusive, was a critical hit and (eventually) a sales success, too. After that, CD Projekt leveled up, moving off of Bioware's engine and creating its own REDengine for 2011's The Witcher 2: Assassins of Kings, The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt, and Cyberpunk 2077.

Of course it's not really a happy anniversary moment. CD Projekt's kind words were prompted by last week's shutdown of BioWare by Electronic Arts, which had the audacity to call itself "the number one publisher in Western HD gaming" while simultaneously admitting that it couldn't figure out what to do with one of the most storied game studios ever.

Even in an industry as riven with layoffs, closures, and general instability as videogames, the end of BioWare felt different and more impactful, sending shockwaves in all directions. Tributes , mourning , and anger followed, and as more anniversaries like this one arrive, I have no doubt we'll see more memories of BioWare, and regrets over its loss, in the future.

items.title: 与乔丹·梅赫纳的一场期待已久的对话
items.summary: The creator of Prince of Persia on why every generation has its defining prince.

content.v: When I started working at PC Gamer in 2014, I began what I didn't realize at the time would become a bit of a ritual. A few weeks before the San Francisco Game Developer's Conference that year, I sent the creator of one of PC gaming's first masterpieces, Prince of Persia, an email asking if he'd be in town. Jordan Mechner politely responded that he wouldn't be making the trip from his home in Paris to San Francisco that year. But I kept trying when the conference rolled back around, thinking maybe this would be the year the stars aligned.

It took a decade, but in 2024 we finally made it happen: Mechner joined a roundtable I hosted alongside other veterans from designing PC games in the '80s and '90s to explore their long careers. Afterward, we talked some more just one-on-one—but in the busy aftermath of the conference, that interview never ended up making its way online.

So here it is now, covering his autobiographical graphic novel, why we may not have seen the last of adventure game The Last Express , and how every generation of fans now has its "own" Prince of Persia.
The many princes of Persia

When this interview was conducted, Ubisoft hadn't yet canceled its remake of Prince of Persia: The Sands of Time , which would've been the first new 3D game in the series in 15 years. The latest 2D game, The Lost Crown , was still fresh, and would be followed not long after our conversation by another 2D game, The Rogue Prince of Persia.
PC Gamer: It's interesting to see different visions of the Prince existing simultaneously now, though obviously Prince of Persia has evolved many times over its history.
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/pn27oLmYkoP3cbsj8nkg5V-1920-80.jpg

Jordan Mechner: I think the Montpellier team made really smart choices with The Lost Crown, and doing Prince of Persia as a 2D Metroidvania, with an emphasis on the fantastic elements and the visual style that harks back to anime. It's also reminiscent of the early 2D Prince of Persia games and of the first Sands of Time.

Even fans of the 2008 Prince of Persia , I think, will find in the mythology and a lot of visual elements things that will make this feel like a Prince of Persia game to them in the best way. With no risk of it being confused with a photorealistic, fully 3D AAA Sands of Time-type game.

I loved the 2008 Prince of Persia. That game got a bad rap: People were like 'it plays itself. You don't have to do anything.' But I thought the fluidity of the movement in that game was just incredible. I loved it.
It's incredible to be part of something that's had so many lives.
Jordan Mechner

And the visuals are absolutely beautiful. There's, there's a lot to like about the 2008 Prince of Persia, and from my vantage point, from what I hear from fans, it has its own devoted, passionate following. Just as much as the Sands of Time trilogy, or the original 2D game.

That's the funny thing about Prince of Persia: That these constituencies are so separate, that there's all three of those. And then there's the Prince of Persia movie, because for many people, especially people who are around 30 years old today, the Prince of Persia movie is Prince of Persia for them, because they weren't the right age to have played any of the games.
There's a new generation of gamers for whom The Lost Crown will be the first Prince of Persia they encounter. It's incredible to be part of something that's had so many lives.
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/oRYTFQXaKqj5UigbsUeXon-1920-80.png
It's slightly surreal for me to hear you say the word 'Metroidvania' because it's such a gamer genre, but it also didn't exist when you made the original.

Of course, I made Prince of Persia about the same time that Metroid and Castlevania were being made. So it's a term that didn't exist, and we didn't have genres in those days in the sense that we do now. I think all of these we would have called platform games or action adventure games.

I don't know if you played Castlevania: Symphony of the Night, or some other version of a Metroidvania? What did it feel like for you having made a platformer that set a lot of precedents, and seeing that genre evolving over the years?

I've never been a Metroidvania player—I would say Prince of Persia: The Lost Crown is actually the first Metroidvania game that I've played and really gotten into as a player. And I'm just enjoying it so much. As a 2d gamer, games that stand out to me are Inside and Limbo, which I thought were really beautiful. I also enjoyed some of the recent Rayman games.
Do you remember much about Prince of Persia 3D? Did you work on that game or consult on that game at all?
That was an internal Broderbund project. So I wasn't on the team, but I knew them.

I had been at Broderbund when I was making Prince of Persia 2: The Shadow and the Flame, which was my last, Broderbund Prince of Persia game. After that I had the idea to do a third episode of the trilogy in 2D. But this was 1993, tthe year of Doom and online multiplayer shooters, and so doing a 2D game just kind of didn't excite publishers, the way it had a year earlier.

So instead of that, I created Smoking Car Productions and The Last Express. While we were making The Last Express, Broderbund, then I think partly looking at Tomb Raider, came around to the idea of doing Prince of Persia as a 3D game. I wasn't involved, but wished them well. And they kept me in the loop.
Do you remember playing that one?
I played the first two levels. It was on PC, and I was a Mac gamer. So it wasn't really my genre, I didn't have a PC that was powerful enough to really enjoy it. So I only saw a bit of it.

Today I hear surprisingly often from gamers that they really enjoyed Prince of Persia 3D and have fond memories of it. So we should probably add that to the list of versions of Prince of Persia that each have their little camp.

I've never played it, but I'm really curious now to go back. It sounds like there wasn't anything you took directly from it. But I'm curious what was going on in that time between Prince of Persia 3D coming out, and you making your own 3D version with Sands of Time?

When I saw Tomb Raider I I was impressed. It blew my mind: it was the first third-person real-time 3D game I'd seen. I was making The Last Express at the time, which was a very different kind of game. But seeing Tomb Raider, I thought 'well we don't need to do Prince of Persia in 3D now. They've just done it. And it's great.'

But seeing Tomb Raider, and then seeing Prince of Persia 3D a few years later, my feeling as a gamer was that I missed the speed and fluidity of 2d gaming. Advancing up to the edge of a block and trying to point yourself in the right direction, and then missing the jump, as a gamer I just had more fun playing the 2D games. Of course, this was a stage in the evolution of 3D. So when I met the Ubisoft Montreal team in 2002, and they pitched the idea of doing a Prince of Persia for the PlayStation 2 generation, my first reservation was, 'how well is this going to work in 3D?'
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/sJYpJnirCXb3YPMSiwPD89-1920-80.jpg
The decision, from Sands of Time to Warrior Within—the mandate to change it from Teen to M was a marketing mandate. It wasn't the team's idea.

content.v: https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2026/10/26/codmw4-1793039849361.jpg

The Call of Duty franchise has now surpassed $40 billion in lifetime franchise revenue in the wake of the launch of its 23rd mainline entry, Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4, which launched last Friday.

Xbox CEO Asha Sharma made the announcement on her X account , posting a graphic showing a bunch of favorable review scores for Modern Warfare 4 with the caption, "One of the most celebrated Call of Duty games in its 24-year history, and now $40B in lifetime franchise revenue. An incredible milestone. Congrats to the Activision team. And to the players, thank you for being with us."

The staying power of the franchise has been remarkably impressive, even if some years' releases are more liked by critics and players than other years. The brand-new Modern Warfare 4 seems to be well-received so far; IGN hasn't finalized its review yet, but reviewer Simon Cardy says, "Modern Warfare 4’s campaign made me feel something for the series again" and "its expansive behind-enemy-lines mission that borrows most of its ideas from the DMZ mode is a real highlight."
For context, Grand Theft Auto 5 alone has pulled in over $10 billion over the past 13 years, and the imminent GTA 6 is estimated to clear $5.2 billion by the end of its first week on sale.
Call of Duty will soon expand beyond just games, however, as Peter Berg's Call of Duty movie is due out in theaters on June 30, 2028 and will explore "the cost of war" for its characters.

items.title: 微软计划裁员 25% 以上
items.summary: An employee buyout offer is reportedly being extended to roughly 60,000 Microsoft employees in the US, UK, Ind

content.v: Microsoft has announced a new "voluntary exit offer" aimed at making drastic cuts to its headcount. A CNN report says roughly 60,000 of the company's employees are eligible for the buyout offer, a number that represents around 27% of its total workforce.

"This offer gives eligible employees who may be considering a future outside the company a new choice to make that transition now with support. It also gives participating organizations another way to adapt their workforce to changing needs," Microsoft chief people officer Amy Coleman said in a memo sent to employees .

"The Voluntary Exit Offer reflects an important part of how we're evolving our approach to change: creating greater flexibility and, where possible, more ways for employees to shape their next chapter. This builds on what we learned earlier this year through the Voluntary Retirement Program."

The CNN report says Microsoft's buyout offer is part of its effort to balance its spending on AI services, and was preceded by its first-ever voluntary buyout program for employees in the US in April, and then layoffs of roughly 4,800 people in July.

The buyout offer is limited to employees in the US, UK, India, and Canada, and not all employees are eligible: Coleman said participation in the program "varies based on each business's priorities, customer commitments and workforce needs." Employees who want to take advantage of the buyout will leave the company on December 31, according to the CNN report.
Whether Xbox is one of the participating businesses was not specified—I've reached out to Xbox to ask and will update if I receive a reply.

items.title: 新的 Windows 11 Insider Experimental 版本增加了无需浏览器即可检查互联网速度的功能
items.summary: A small change, but a handy one.

content.v: If you are part of the Windows 11 Insider program, you may have finally received the option to test your internet speed directly from Quick Settings in the latest experimental build. That means no more going to a browser to see if your new broadband package is as speedy as advertised.

Those using Insider Experimental build 26340.9767 can simply click on Quick Settings and scroll down to see a speed test button (via Windows Latest ). You can also find the network icon in the system tray, right-click it, and then select "Test internet speed". This will give you your download and upload speeds.

Up until now, Windows 11 users have been able to access an internet speed test from Windows settings, but clicking on it redirects you to a browser and then runs the test via Bing. It's a small barrier but still an annoying hurdle to get to a fairly simple tool.

Alongside this, Preview Build 26340.9767 adds feature flags (so you can filter your machine by which options are enabled / disabled), Quick Settings now gives access to mobile phones, it adds a Magnifier keyboard shortcut, it gives an easier way to access your Microsoft 365 subscription, and a few other things.

If you'd like to get access to the latest Insider Preview Builds, you can simply register to become an insider , then go into your Windows update settings, and select the latest option. Naturally, there's some risk with trying out developing tech, and the experience likely won't be as smooth as the traditional Windows build, but you do get access to some new features early.
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/yEMK6QNhtXcquwrZJYVkoB-1920-80.jpg

As well as this, there's technically no guarantee that any Insider updates will actually come to the stable build of Windows 11. Insiders are sort of like beta testers for Windows software, and if enough feedback suggests the implementation is poor, Microsoft could listen to that and remove it from future updates.

Still, being able to check your internet connection speed without accessing a browser feels like an uncontroversial update. Skipping any barriers to get that information quicker feels beneficial to the end user, and I can certainly see myself using it next time I need to test it. Or, most likely, if I want to complain about how slow my speed is going on a given day.
