items.title: 现在，一整套 Steam PC 游戏都可以在越狱的 PlayStation 5 上本地运行，包括《传送门》、《Left 4 Dead 2》等等
items.summary: I never thought I'd see the day.

content.v: What a time to be alive. Gamers are starting to play Steam games locally on jailbroken PlayStation 5 consoles, thanks to several projects that aim to bring PC gaming to the Sony-loving masses. One such project is Playden for PS5 , which was made publicly available earlier this month.

The program functions as a Steam launcher, but also creates a private Windows environment via prospero-win, a port of Wine for PlayStation 5 (via Videocardz ). The software has support for up to Direct3D 11 through DXVK and Direct3D 12 games through VKD3D-Proton, and includes a separate runtime kit for the graphics drivers, along with specific app shells for the games themselves.

"It downloads a game, prepares it, and hands it to a separate PS5 app made for that game. That app starts Wine with the game's settings," says the readme on the project's GitHub page. "Because each game is its own app, it has its own tile on the PS5 Home screen, and it is isolated: its files, settings and crashes stay inside it."

Reddit user Cevap has posted a video of their jailbroken PS5 playing Portal locally . "Game runs as you expect," says Cevap. "Only issue being you can’t use a mouse cursor, nor can you press ESC to go to the options. Otherwise basic controls work. What an amazing project, thank you!"

In the case of Playden for PS5, the GitHub page stresses that the software is in an early alpha state, so it's probably best not to expect too much from it at this stage. The compatible games list is pretty chonky, though, including some pretty big hitters. Just be prepared for crashes if you give it a go yourself.

It must also be mentioned that, aside from the risks of jailbreaking a PS5 in the first place, users also need to log in to their official Steam accounts to use the software. "Valve does not support third-party clients," say the devs "We know of no account problems from this, but the risk is yours to accept."

It's also quite an involved process to get it working by the looks of things, so this is probably one for advanced users. Still, I guess I can chalk this up as "things I thought I'd never see." An increasingly long list in 2026, it seems.

items.title: Valve 表示将研究此事后不到十分钟就向 Steam Frame 内核添加了 CD-ROM 支持
items.summary: That was fast.

content.v: You can truly never anticipate how one might use their tech. After a Steam Frame owner asked why the VR headset didn't work with their detachable disc drive , Valve developer gaberow said they were looking into it—and patched in kernel support mere minutes later.
As spotted by Tom's Hardware , AiodensGhost asked for the feature on October 18, gaberowe responded on October 19, then made the commit to the Steam Frame kernel in less than ten minutes.

If you're wondering why someone would want CD-ROM support, AiodensGhost says, "I wanted to use my Steam Frame to be able to watch a movie on the road, and thought it was no big deal to use the detachable disc drive I had on my computer."

They continue, "Turns out that the Frame cannot power the player and even if it could it lacks the drivers to read a disc. Valve, this not only killed my ability to watch a movie, IT KILLED MY ABILITY TO INSTALL MY ABANDONWARE FROM 2006. You don't sell NFS Carbon anymore."

The mention of Need for Speed Carbon is interesting here, as it suggests one might opt to boot up a game on the Steam Frame from a CD-ROM drive, rather than streaming one from a library. Carbon is not officially on Steam (or any legal digital storefronts as far as I can see), so the only way to legally play some games on the Steam Frame would be via an old disc.
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/vY4ztJVBw6dNr9Zr4sVMMT-1920-80.jpg

The Steam Frame does seem primarily built for use in VR games, but given its comfort and screen, it would make sense why one might enjoy it for 2D games and movies. CD-ROM support would make the device a little more versatile.

One thing that is worth noting here is that kernel-level support doesn't mean that all Steam Frame units will officially gain the feature. It means Valve could implement the change in a future Steam Frame update should it want to. Given the public reply from a developer and the kernel change, my money is on official support arriving in the future, but Valve could always opt not to do so.

Should you want to add it yourself, you can install the kernel on your device via the ' Deckard Linux no oopsies ' repo, instead of waiting for any sort of official update. But I'd hazard a guess that those looking for disc drive support are fairly few in the first place.
